  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - JANUARY 2026  
  REINFORCEMENT LEARNING [CSE_4028]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                    Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                 Model how the key elements of Reinforcement Learning work together in enabling an autonomous        (5)  
  robot to navigate a maze.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)            Develop the application of Positive and Negative Reinforcement in designing a game-playing agent (3)  
  that learns optimal moves through feedback.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)            Identify the limitations and scope of the Reinforcement Learning problem when applied to real-world (2)  
  decision-making systems.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                                                                                                                     (5)  
  
  
  A)

  C)            Identify how the probability mass function (PMF) is used to describe the behavior of a discrete     (2)  
  random variable and determine the probability of specific outcomes.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3)                 Analyze how the Action-Value Methods are applied to solve the n-Armed Bandit Problem,               (5)  
  highlighting how different approaches such as the sample-average and incremental methods  
  A)            estimate the action values and influence the exploration-exploitation trade-off.  
  
  Page #1

Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)         Apply how the unified notation is applied to represent both episodic and continuing tasks within a    (3)  
  finite Markov Decision Process, emphasizing the role of the discount factor in connecting the two  
  formulations.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)         Apply the concept of Upper-Confidence-Bound (UCB) Variables to select actions in a reinforcement (2)  
  learning task, balancing exploration and exploitation during decision-making.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)              Apply the concepts of optimality and approximation can be applied in a robotic path-planning          (5)  
  scenario, where the agent must learn near-optimal policies under limited computational resources  
  A)         and incomplete environment knowledge.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)         Compare the processes of Policy Iteration and Value Iteration in Dynamic Programming,              (3)  
  emphasizing their computational steps, convergence characteristics, and effectiveness in obtaining  
  the optimal policy.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)         Develop an example of a finite MDP where the agent optimizes long-term returns to achieve a           (2)  
  specific goal state.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)              Compare On-Policy and Off-Policy Monte Carlo Control methods, emphasizing how importance              (5)  
  sampling enables the off-policy approach to learn an optimal policy while following a different  
  A)         behavior policy.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)         Apply how Actor-Critic Methods can be modified using eligibility traces to enhance learning           (3)  
  efficiency, enabling faster policy and value function updates in dynamic reinforcement learning  
  environment  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)         Develop a short expression for the R-Learning value update, highlighting how it differs from          (2)  
  standard Q-Learning.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
